title: Ex-PM says Sudan risks partition amid US ceasefire push
gist: Former Sudanese Prime Minister Abdalla Hamdok told Al-Monitor that Sudan risks de facto partition unless the US-led ceasefire push is paired with an inclusive political process, citing the trauma of South Sudan's 2011 secession, and urged US sanctions carrying 'personal consequences' for the warring sides.

insights.claim: Former Sudanese PM Abdalla Hamdok warns Sudan risks de facto partition unless the US-led ceasefire push is paired with an inclusive political process.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: A ceasefire-only deal that freezes front lines could entrench a divided Sudan, with lasting implications for Red Sea security and regional stability.
insights.quote: Sudan risks de facto partition unless the US-led push for a ceasefire is paired with an inclusive political process
insights.locator: WASHINGTON — Sudan risks de facto partition

insights.claim: Hamdok said Sudanese fear partition because the country already 'lost a third' of its territory with South Sudan's 2011 secession after an independence referendum.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Historical precedent makes partition a politically salient risk rather than a theoretical one.
insights.quote: having gone through previous partitioning. We lost a third of our country

insights.claim: Hamdok argues the political process must not take a back seat to the ceasefire track in US mediation.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Signals civilian Sudanese pushback against a security-first US approach, which could complicate or slow a deal.
insights.quote: We don't want to see a situation where the political process is taking a backseat
insights.locator: WASHINGTON — Sudan risks de facto partition

insights.claim: Hamdok called for the United States to impose sanctions that would carry 'personal consequences' for Sudan's warring sides.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Points toward individual-level sanctions on Sudanese military leaders as a possible next US policy lever.
insights.quote: impose sanctions that would carry “personal consequences” for the warring sides
